events.title: Más Arte Más Acción: Around A Tree
events.description: Newly installed for continuing use after its original EAF24 installation, Around a Tree is a site for gathering, dialogue, and exchange, created by Colombian foundation Más Arte Más Acción. The table, which has travelled globally in many forms, invites visitors to pause, reflect, and engage with pressing conversations on the climate crisis. Surrounding a Portuguese Oak sapling, the table is made from a 164-year-old Lebanese Cedar felled in the Garden due to needle blight, embodying climate resilience. Seated around it, visitors connect: with each other, with nature, and with new perspectives.

events.title: Giants
events.description: Giants is an immersive exhibition featuring large-scale, sculptural installations which bring giant prehistoric animals to life alongside life-sized models, fossils and nearly complete skeletons. The exhibition showcases the enormous but often overlooked creatures that roamed the Earth after the extinction of the dinosaurs, embarking on a journey through time, from 66 million years ago to the present day. Combining design and natural science, Giants introduces animals including Paraceratherium, the largest land mammal ever known to have walked the Earth, and Titanoboa cerrejonensis, the world’s longest ever snake. Developed by the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences and toured by Nomad Exhibitions.

events.title: Earth Matters
events.description: In Earth Matters , over 30 artists delve into soil to reveal its brilliance, beauty, and fragility, celebrating the 300th birthday of ‘the father of modern geology’, James Hutton. Recognised for his radical exploration of the ground beneath us, Hutton is an Edinburgh-born geologist, farmer and writer who revolutionised our understanding of Earth’s creation. Featuring work from artists Wilhelmina Barns-Graham, Joan Eardley, Sekai Machache, Alberta Whittle, and more, the exhibition draws on illustrations by Hutton’s collaborator John Clerk of Eldin and earth itself, revealing the soil’s hidden depths, its past, and its future. A creative partnership with Susanna Beaumont, Design Exhibition Scotland. Supported by Postcode Lottery players and Edinburgh Geological Society, with special thanks to the James Hutton Institute. Part of Edinburgh Science Festival, RSA200 and James Hutton Tercentenary 2026.

events.title: The Edwardians: Age of Elegance
events.description: The Edwardians: Age of Elegance explores the opulence and glamour of the Edwardian age through the lives and tastes of two of Britain’s most fashionable royal couples: King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra, and King George V and Queen Mary. From their family lives and personal collecting, to their glittering social circles and spectacular royal events, the exhibition documents British royalty from Edward and Alexandra’s wedding in 1863, up to the end of the First World War. The exhibition features works by the most renowned contemporary artists of the period, including Carl Fabergé, Frederic Leighton, Edward Burne-Jones, Rosa Bonheur and John Singer Sargent.

events.title: Jean F. Watson: An Artistic Legacy
events.description: Since the 1960s, the Jean F. Watson Bequest Fund has enabled the City of Edinburgh to acquire more than 1000 Scottish artworks. This exhibition celebrates Jean F. Watson’s vision and generosity, showcasing a selection of historic and contemporary artworks from the collection, including work from Arthur Melville, JD Fergusson, Joan Eardley, Eduardo Paolozzi, and more.

events.title: Moira Salt + Olivia Priya Foster: PLATFORM
events.description: Developing work as part of a long-term residency with the festival, Moira Salt and Olivia Priya Foster are the first awardees of EAF’s reimagined PLATFORM opportunity for early career artists. Moira Salt is a trans-disciplinary artist, working fluidly across film, sound, performance, textiles, and text, chasing diasporic belonging and myths of her ancestry through water, land, and body. Olivia Priya Foster is an interdisciplinary artist exploring rurality in Scotland through the lens of their South Asian and Scottish heritage, navigating questions of cultural identity, belonging, and place. Both artists will use 2026 for in-depth, behind-the-scenes development, before showcasing their new work in a festival exhibition in 2027. About PLATFORM 2026 debuts a reimagined PLATFORM award, an evolution of EAF’s longstanding programme supporting early-career artists. This new iteration responds to the changing landscape of visual arts in Scotland, offering more expansive, sustainable support. Artists work with the festival over an 18-month period, developing their practice with the time, space, and security to explore, including through an in person residency at the Hugo Burge Foundation. Supported by the Paul Hamlyn Foundation, Idlewild Trust, the Hugo Burge Foundation and Scottish Government’s EXPO Fund.

events.title: Wendy McMurdo: The Digital Mirror
events.description: The Digital Mirror spans 20 years of Wendy McMurdo’s photographic reflections on childhood, the digital world, learning and make-believe. Working at the forefront of developments in digital photography, McMurdo has blazed a trail in the experimental use of computers and digital tools in photography, from the early days of computer-based learning in schools, to the growth of the internet and networked gaming. The digital landscape is changing faster than ever with children spending more time online, and technology offers limitless possibilities for imaginative learning. Her largest exhibition to date, The Digital Mirror offers a fascinating response to the impact of technology on learning and play in childhood.

events.title: Porty Pride Screening: Fairy Heights + Alasdair
events.description: Join EAF and Bona Varda on Sunday 7 June for a two-part screening event sharing local Scottish queer histories and acts of community resilience. Fairy Heights is a powerful short documentary exploring the Grassmarket housing block in Edinburgh, where queer residents built a vital network of care during the AIDS crisis. Through interviews with former residents, the film brings to life a community defined by solidarity and chosen family. Presented in partnership with Lavender Menace. Alasdair is a preview of an intimate documentary, offering a glimpse into the life of Alasdair, Gaelic broadcaster, translator and writer. Set against the striking landscape of the Isle of Skye, the short film follows Alasdair on a deeply moving 10-day journey to summit to Sgùrr Alasdair, the highest peak in the Inner Hebrides, reflecting with honesty and depth on the realities of living with AIDS. This special film was found after 35 years through the support of David McLean (Bona Varda), following a search prompted by EAF’s World Aids Day event on 1 December 2026. EAF will be selling a limited run of screen printed ‘Support Your Local Queer Archive’ t-shirts, raising money for Lavender Menace Queer Books Archive’s ongoing Save Lavender Menace fundraiser. events.title: Katie Paterson: Afterlife
events.description: Afterlife is a sculptural installation by internationally acclaimed Scottish artist Katie Paterson, comprised of nearly 200 amulets. Each is created with materials sourced from endangered landscapes and fragile ecosystems, exploring themes of deep time, geology, and the environment. Coming to Scotland for the first time after its initial commission for Folkestone Triennial 2025, Afterlife prompts us to consider the legacies we leave for future generations.

events.title: Elizabeth Blackadder: A Life in Colour
events.description: A Life in Colour celebrates the enduring relationship between Scottish painter Elizabeth Blackadder and Dovecot Studios with a display of co-created textile works. Over a five-decade creative partnership, the textiles studio produced over 30 tapestries and hand-tufted rugs which translated the artist’s distinctive visual language into richly textured forms. The exhibition highlights the vitality of Blackadder’s palette and its common language across different mediums. The exhibition will also feature a display of Dovecot’s newest tufted rug, created after Blackadder’s work. Presented in partnership with The Royal Scottish Academy. Exhibition forms part of RSA200: Celebrating Together.

events.title: Songs of Innocence & Experience, part II
events.description: Songs of Innocence & Experience, part II celebrates the Caribbean artist Frank Walter through the work of 20 artists who have either responded directly to his paintings, or whose own work has something to say in conversation with his. The exhibition features work from Frank Walter himself, as well as artists Beatrice Arraes, David Austen, Hayley Barker, Alvaro Barrington, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Robert Coutelas, Andrew Cranston, Peter Doig, Sky Glabush, Nick Goss, Mia Kokkoni, Aubrey Levinthal, John Maclean, Elizabeth Magill, John Joseph Mitchell, Christopher Colm Morrin, Craig Murray-Orr, Cassi Namoda, Andrew Pierre Hart, Ellen Siebers, Hiroshi Sugito, Tal R, and Rose Wylie. The exhibition is shown with thanks to Frank Walter’s family and consulting curator Dr Barbara Paca OBE.

events.title: Anne Hardy
events.description: British sculptor Anne Hardy transforms Talbot Rice Gallery’s Georgian Gallery into a single immersive space, with sculptures made from cast elements, found materials and earth drawings. In this large-scale installation, Hardy constructs landscapes that are both human and post-human by animating the gallery with light, sound, data, and scenography. By grafting seemingly incompatible contexts into another, she considers how our bodies respond to space and sensory stimuli, creating an atmosphere that is responsive and alive with energy. Supported by Edinburgh College of Art, Creative Scotland, and Henry Moore Foundation. Presented in association with Edinburgh International Festival and EAF.

events.title: Sandra George: Start from the Level
events.description: Photographer Sandra George devoted her life to working with communities, documenting and developing vital social-action projects in Edinburgh for over thirty years. The legacy she has left is a first-hand social history through her distinctive lens. In partnership with Craigmillar Now, Start from the Level includes over 200 photographs, showcasing George’s powerful and empowering archive.

events.title: Decolonising the Outdoors: Tectonics Book Launch
events.description: we are fragments / scattered in the folds / tracing memories across fault lines Join Decolonising the Outdoors and EAF to celebrate the launch of new artist book Tectonics . As part of their commission for EAF25, artist Aileen Angsutorn Lees explored our connections to the outdoors and how our surroundings affect what our bodies carry. This 18-month project comprised visual artwork, research, workshops and community engagement. How do we move away from the margins? What does it mean to reclaim the outdoors? Layering the past, present and future, Tectonics is an archive where voices converge. The artist weaves their writing and artwork with community voices and historical texts. Across 35 hand-bound, riso and screen-printed pages, narratives are interrogated; our stories held. The launch includes readings on the theme of reclamation, as well as an opportunity for attendees to add an additional, personal page to their book – creating their own ‘tectonic plate’ in response to prompts. Books will be available to buy on the night. About the artist Aileen Angsutorn Lees is a writer, photographer and poet. She is the founder of Decolonising The Outdoors, a creative and community project which dismantles narratives of dominating land and extracting nature. Tectonics is created and designed in collaboration with Elle Haswell as part of EAF’s Civic Programme. events.title: Esther Castle: Abundant Parts
events.description: Abundant Parts is a newly commissioned installation by Esther Castle, an other-worldly garden which draws symbolic connections between the non-normative body and weeds, often considered an undesirable presence and removed by gardeners. The installation includes surreal elements, indicating a state of slippage relevant to both a failure of our bodies’ defence systems and the gardener’s futile attempt to control and contain the natural world. The work has been developed through ESW’s Hawthornvale Mentorship Scheme.

events.title: Richard Maguire: There is no beginning, as there is no end
events.description: There is no beginning, as there is no end is a new solo commission by Richard Maguire: the first in the Time + Space early-career artist programme. Primarily working in drawing and sculpture, Maguire’s practice considers power relations through histories and representations of race and sexuality between Britain and South Asia. Referring to archives and material culture, Maguire explores the legacy of historical systems of oppression.

events.title: Eva Rothschild: The Void Presses The Wall
events.description: The Void Presses The Wall is a major exhibition by London-based Irish artist Eva Rothschild, whose work grows out of a commitment to sculpture’s capacity to create bodily encounters in space . Her sculptures are born of the city and redolent of the urban landscape. Some, cast or constructed in bronze, plaster or steel, are supported on plinths, ‘behaving’ like sculptures ‘should’, while others stretch, twist, balance, or form whole environments in concrete, polystyrene, cotton and canvas that the viewer must negotiate. Her work creates a constant push-and-pull of the power dynamic between audience and object, drawing attention to how we occupy space. Supported by the Henry Moore Foundation, and the generosity of the Eva Rothschild Supporter’s Circle.

events.title: Costume Couture: Sixty Years of Cosprop
events.description: Featuring many iconic period costumes from film, television, and theatre, Costume Couture celebrates the legendary costume house Cosprop. From A Room with a View to Pride and Prejudice , Meryl Streep to Maggie Smith, Cosprop has become synonymous with dressing iconic characters in award-winning films and television. The exhibition celebrates 60 years of creativity since Cosprop’s founding by Oscar and BAFTA-winning designer John Bright, giving a unique opportunity to see behind the scenes, with sketches, accessories, and iconic costumes.

events.title: Rachel McBrinn + Jonathan Webb: Study for North Bridge
events.description: Study for North Bridge is a new moving image commission which responds to Edinburgh’s North Bridge. The film places the bridge’s current restoration in its historical context, from its original build in the 1760s, to the city developing around it. Commissioned by City of Edinburgh Council, the film commemorates one of Edinburgh’s most historically significant landmarks.

events.title: Etchingroom1: Unexpected Trip
events.description: Ukrainian duo Kristina Yarosh and Anna Khodkova, who work under the name etchingroom1, created a mural during a residency in 2023, which is now displayed on the Beacon Tower at ESW and connects to their new exhibition at Edinburgh Printmakers. The work taps into a long lineage of political murals as expression of collective struggles and messages of hope amongst terrible events. It is a work of art and activism, emblematic of our time which speaks of the artists’ experiences of conflict and of their resilience. The mural is viewable every day from near the cafe patio.

events.title: Jamie Fitzpatrick: Memorials to Sausage Politics
events.description: Memorials to Sausage Politics is a new exhibition by Jamie Fitzpatrick exploring debates around post-colonial public statuary. Developed through residencies at Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop and Edinburgh Printmakers, it presents new prints and printed sculptures that reimagine monuments as comic, monstrous forms, questioning their symbolism and place within Scotland’s civic landscape.

events.title: Kate Downie: Grasslands
events.description: Grasslands is a major exhibition combining drawing, experimental printmaking, painting, and film, inspired by close observation of Scotland’s diverse grassland environments: from the Tay Estuary reed beds to the wind-swept coasts of Shetland. Downie’s practice focuses on the often overlooked, revealing the complexity and resilience of grasses; grass is everywhere, its roots binding the land together. Influenced since youth by Dürer’s Great Piece of Turf, Downie continues to explore new visual languages in search of a way to transcend the familiar and elevate the ordinary into something both intimate and monumental.

events.title: Stephen Bird: Looping States of Mind: Circular Thoughts
events.description: In Looping States of Mind , contemporary artist Stephen Bird explores the entanglements between environment, place, and human experience through layered narratives, dualities, and paradoxes. Blending satire and social commentary, Bird creates intricate, provocative compositions that expand ceramic traditions through storytelling, humour, and sharp cultural observation. Developed through recent travels in Scotland and Europe, the work engages with cultural exchange, political histories, and artistic traditions, from Dundee’s connections with Palestine, to encounters with historic collections in Rome.

events.title: Jillian Edelstein: Among People
events.description: Spanning four decades of work, Among People is a major survey of internationally renowned documentary and portrait photographer Jillian Edelstein. Born in South Africa and now based in London, Edelstein has spent more than forty years documenting people, communities across the world, and defining moments of contemporary history. The first major exhibition of Edelstein’s work, Among People reveals the artist’s distinctive ability to capture both everyday lives and pivotal moments with empathy and insight.

events.title: Gwen John: Strange Beauties
events.description: Strange Beauties is the first major retrospective in over forty years dedicated to Welsh painter Gwen John (1876—1939). One of the first generation of women to receive a formal art education, John studied at the Slade School of Art in London, before settling in Paris. The exhibition showcases celebrated oil paintings and rarely seen drawings, ranging from her early years in Wales, through to experimental late works inspired by John’s religious beliefs, French modernism, and her surroundings in the Parisian suburb of Meudon. Marking 150 years since the artist’s birth, Strange Beauties offers a fresh new perspective on Gwen John’s work and artistic legacy. Developed by Amgueddfa Cymru in partnership with National Galleries of Scotland, Yale Center for British Art, and the National Museum of Women in the Arts, Washington DC.

events.title: Lee McCormack: A Magic Lantern
events.description: A Magic Lantern is the first solo exhibition by Niddrie photographer and former community worker Lee McCormack. Her powerful and sensitive photographs capture domestic scenes and social action between the late 1970s to early 2000s . McCormack trained with the Film Workshop Trust and went on to work for Craigmillar Festival Society, Magic Lantern Van, Womenzone and Women’s Aid, engaging with diverse groups across Scotland. This collection of personal and joyful images offer a behind the scenes view of her life, and the community and art projects she was involved in.

events.title: Catherine Opie: To Be Seen
events.description: To Be Seen is the UK’s first major museum exhibition of work by American artist Catherine Opie. Visitors are invited to discover powerful photographic portraits of Opie’s mentors and collaborators, queer communities, children, surfers, high school footballers, and political crowds. The exhibition includes nearly 80 portraits by Opie, shown alongside a selection of portraits from Scotland’s national collection. Journeying through over three decades of Opie’s work, the exhibition questions representations of home, intimacy, and family, exploring politics, identity, and power structures. In partnership with the National Portrait Gallery.

events.description: Join Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop for Sculpture Saturdays: free, drop-in workshops where families are invited to explore, imagine, and make together. The workshops will take creative prompts and wide range of everyday materials as the basis for making artworks. Participants are encouraged to work alone or collaboratively. events.title: Katie Paterson + Richard Maguire BSL Tour
events.description: Join Collective Gallery for a BSL Tour of Katie Paterson’s exhibition Afterlife and Richard Maguire’s exhibition There is No Beginning, As There Is No End . This Deaf-led tour will be hosted by Trudi Collier and will offer BSL visitors the opportunity to learn more about the exhibitions. There will be refreshments to wrap up the session, with opportunity to discuss the exhibitions with Trudi and other attendees. Trudi will be joined by an interpreter for this event.

events.title: Del LaGrace Volcano: Love Bites Back
events.description: Love Bites Back focuses on a pivotal period of dyke photography produced by Del LaGrace Volcano, between 1982 and 1995. Developed through Volcano’s early explorations of queer identity, BDSM culture, and embodied politics, the exhibition offers an intimate and confrontational portrait of communities navigating desire, power, and self-representation. Presenting never-before-seen work from Volcano’s time in Edinburgh, the works trace the development of the artist’s striking visual language during a concentrated moment of experimentation: challenging traditional understandings of gender and sexuality, affirming the erotic and authorial agency of the people that appear in them. Love Bites Back is the sister exhibition of Sensual / Mutual, showing Volcano’s earlier work from the 1980s at London gallery Auto Italia . Volcano’s photography will also appear on billboards across Edinburgh in August, in partnership with BUILDHOLLYWOOD Scotland. Event Info: → This exhibition is across Galleries 1 + 2 of EAF @ 92. events.title: Emii Alrai: Guardian
events.description: Guardian is a monumental new sculptural commission by Emii Alrai, exploring the cultural power and contested political histories of archaeological ruins. Installed atop Calton Hill, the work takes the form of a colossal, fragmented relic inspired by mythical icons of ancient civilisations, in direct dialogue with the unfinished National Monument of Scotland, often called “Edinburgh’s Disgrace.” Drawing on Alrai’s British-Iraqi heritage, Guardian references Sumerian divine beings the Lamassu, while engaging with histories of excavation, displacement, and empire. Its vivid blue patina and exposed armature evoke both preservation and decay. Following its commission for Bold Tendencies in 2025, the work is built upon and ruptured into ghostly fragments, proposing a monument that acknowledges fracture, and reimagines how the past is held in the present. events.title: Metal Memories: Sounds of the Palestinian Streets
events.description: Update: This installation at the Palestine Museum has now closed. We look forward to welcoming you to our other events happening across the city for the final days of EAF26. This new exhibition is presented by Mo’min Swaitat of Majazz Project and Palestinian Sound Archive. The exhibition features the installation of a mobile loudspeaker system often used at Bedouin weddings, looping a sonic mix of rare recordings. The field-recorded tapes share artists’ contributions to Palestinian history and cultural heritage, with a focus on wedding music and dance. More than 25,000 weddings are held each year in the West Bank, where hundreds of attendees gather to share music and do dabka and dahiya: two fast-paced, stomping folk dances common throughout the region. Haddaya, (or debates, challenges) also form the soundtrack of weddings of Palestinians from every class in society, combining artists’ improvised spoken word, a moving metal sound system, and the clapping of hundreds of attendees. Metal Memories is a celebration of Palestinian and Bedouin wedding culture which invites us to imagine Palestine through sound, heard as never before. events.title: Sadao Hasegawa: Carnal Desires
events.description: Carnal Desires is a rare exhibition of work by Sadao Hasegawa, revealing the under-recognised and largely unseen work of one of post-war Japan’s most influential gay fetish artists. Celebrated for his depiction of hypermasculine forms, Hasegawa’s paintings blend eroticism with pan-Asian folklore, science fiction, and popular culture, imagining a universe where chiselled men encounter mythic creatures, hybrid animals, and divine bodies unbound by earthly limits. While his illustrations were originally published in gay magazines across the US, UK, and Australia, much of his work has remained virtually inaccessible outside Japan. This is the first exhibition of Hasegawa’s work in Scotland at this scale, featuring unearthed pieces from the archives of Tokyo’s Gallery Naruyama, many of which have never before been shown in the UK. Carnal Desires invites audiences into a provocative and fantastical queer cosmos, celebrating desire in its most unrestrained form. events.title: Tell Me About It: Hard Labour
events.description: Tell Me About It: Hard Labour creates a space for direct one-to-one conversations with people who have lived experience of sex work. Created in partnership with Scotland for Decrim, a grassroots campaign fighting for the full decriminalisation of sex work in Scotland, Tell Me About It , is one part of a larger multi-art form project, Hard Labour , in partnership with Arika. Extending into the city, a streets-based poster campaign with BUILDHOLLYWOOD Scotland transforms public space into a site of reflection and solidarity, making sex workers’ histories, voices, and creative practices visible in everyday life. Accompanying events, both for sex workers only and the public, explore subjects from church occupations to intimate narratives of survival, care, and resilience. For the first time, Ellis Jackson Kroese of Trans Masc Studies presents their research alongside a hoard of alternative trans artefacts, a curated selection of books and zines, and a dedicated workspace for visitors’ own use. History is a Home pictures queer history as a place of belonging and connection, inviting transcestors past to inform and transform our present and future. events.title: Christine Borland + Dovecot Studios: The Edinburgh Seven Tapestry
events.description: Permanently installed at the Edinburgh Futures Institute, the Edinburgh Seven Tapestry commemorates the first women to matriculate at any British university. Designed by Christine Borland and created by Dovecot Studios, the tapestry triptych was made using a combination of traditional and modern materials and techniques. Its organic shapes are based on cellular structure in motion. Commissioned by Dovecot Studios, with funding from Sir Ewan and Lady Brown.

events.title: Etchingroom1: What A Wonderful Day In A Wonderful World
events.description: Created by Ukrainian duo Etchingroom1 (Kristina Yarosh and Anna Khodkova), this mural is a message of hope against the background of terrible events: a work of art and activism which speaks of the artists’ experiences of conflict.

events.title: Kate Power
events.description: River sounds, rave beats and folk singing resonate within Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop’s Beacon Tower, in this new sound installation by artist Kate Power. The installation foregrounds listening as a bodily practice that moves across skin, bone, fluid and atmosphere. Power’s research explores how sound is sensed through the body and how shared experiences of vibration and rhythm bring bodies into relation. Her work considers listening as a somatic practice shaped by attention, environment, and the thresholds of what can be heard. The work was developed during a residency exchange with Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop’s partners in Quebec, Fonderie Darling and Gare de Matapédia, and Hospitalfield in the UK. Supported by Quartier Éphémère, Fonderie Darling, Gare de Matapédia, Hospitalfield; Conseil des arts de Montréal, Creative Scotland, British Council Scotland, Conseil des arts et des lettres du Quebec, St Andrews Society of Montréal, Quebec Government Office in London, City of Edinburgh Council.

events.title: The Marks Left Behind: Generative Artwork
events.description: The Marks Left Behind is an algorithmic artwork by Dave Bowes of Great Snakes AV, displayed on the Portal, the creative screen at the north entrance. Small data from forgotten interactions with the building reveal its untold stories. Every building holds stories beyond those recorded in archives. They are written instead through countless everyday encounters: footsteps, pauses, conversations, and the quiet movements of people passing through its spaces. Over time, these fleeting moments become part of the building itself. One of the richest records of this hidden history is found in the marks left behind. The worn paths on a staircase, the subtle traces of repeated movement, and the almost invisible evidence of human presence reveal patterns that no single individual intended to create. Together, these accumulated imprints tell an evolving story of the people who have inhabited this place. This installation transforms those passing moments into a living artwork. The LED wall captures anonymised data generated by visitors as they move through the building, creating a composition that is entirely unique each day. While algorithmic in its operation, the work is shaped not by artificial intelligence or pre-determined mathematical systems alone, but by the collective presence of the building’s occupants. As you contribute to the work, you’ve become an unwitting co-author of its continually changing form. About the Artist Dave Bowes, who also works under the name Great Snakes AV, is a Scottish mixed-media artist. His practice explores consciousness, presence, memory and the hidden traces we leave behind. Central to his work is the creation of generative systems that combine the structured logic of computation with a more intuitive, human-centred artistic process. It is within the dialogue between these two approaches that his artworks emerge. Co-commissioned by Aberdeen Performing Arts and New Media Scotland’s Alt-w Fund with investment from Creative Scotland and the University of Edinburgh.

events.title: Where We Are
events.description: In the Anthea Bond Exhibition Room, Edinburgh International Book Festival’s show Where We Are celebrates work by local participants in their Communities Programme, with illustrations from Edinburgh College of Art students.

events.title: EAF Welcome Space
events.description: The EAF Welcome Space at Brown’s of Leith offers a place to arrive, pause, and begin exploring the festival programme. As well as a touch point for information, the Welcome Space is home to our Festival Shop, stocked with limited edition artist wearables, curated books, and mementoes of EAF26.

events.title: Scotland’s Collection at Modern One
events.description: Modern One presents 120 years of world-class modern and contemporary art for free. Visitors can experience outstanding artworks by Michael Armitage, Salvador Dalí, Peter Doig, Inka Essenhigh, Jasleen Kaur, Roy Lichtenstein, Everlyn Nicodemus, Dorothea Tanning and many more. Themed and in-focus displays explore diverse creative perspectives on environment, identity, and the complexity of our inner lives, including the radical and subversive Surrealism: Picturing the Strange . With beautiful sculpture gardens, welcoming spaces and room to reflect, Modern One offers rich, uplifting and thought-provoking encounters with influential artists and their ideas. The collection is yours to discover.

events.title: Fair Play
events.description: Fair Play is a collaborative exhibition by local children and the wider community, presenting an evolving fairground environment of sculptures across Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop’s North Lab and Courtyard. Bringing together imagined rides, attractions and playful structures, the project invites participants to collectively imagine and build their own fairgrounds together. The initial sculptures were created through workshops with Primary 5 pupils from partner schools as part of Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop’s Schools Programme. Fair Play continues to evolve through contributions from families and visitors at drop-in Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop’s Sculpture Saturdays .

events.title: Off the Charts
events.description: In this group exhibition, four emerging artists selected for the inaugural Blackie House Graduate Awards respond to a selection of maps, globes and books held in the Blackie House Library and Museum. Artists Milly Toplis, Eve Giltinan Allais, Elena Nieva, and Alyth Krzyzanowska will chart Scotland’s land and seascapes: its hills, mountains and valleys, its lochs, rivers and canals, its paths and roads, its windmills and oil rigs, coastline and islands. In the age of GPS, the new commissions consider what positions creative minds occupy in and around these natural and man-made features, finding their points of orientation across various media. Told individually and collectively, their stories will take shape in the Blackie House’s unique satellite space: a 250-year-old garage.

events.title: Sgàire Wood: In Pride, In Piety, In Vigilance
events.description: In this new commission, Glasgow-based Irish artist Sgàire Wood draws on traditional heraldic imagery to examine notions of heritage, belonging, and the violence embedded in visual culture. With its origins in drag, fashion photography and multi-artform nightlife scenes, Wood’s practice is concerned with the layers of meaning behind everyday images, visual performances of identity, pop-cultural symbolism, authenticity, and artifice. In this new work, she positions urban wildlife and mythic heraldic creatures as representations of the precarity and oppression faced by minorities amidst the rise of fascism. Wood critically questions these systems of belief and our current political urgencies, all while leaving room for humour, hope and the possibilities of belonging and solidarity.

events.title: In Conversation: Katie Paterson + Ingrid Moye
events.description: Join artist Katie Paterson in conversation with Ingrid Moye from Berlin/Mexico City based architects, Zeller & Moye, as they discuss their long-term collaboration. Their most recent collaboration is Afterlife , Paterson’s latest work, currently on display in Collective Gallery. Afterlife is a sculptural installation comprised of nearly 200 amulets. Each is created with materials sourced from endangered landscapes and fragile ecosystems, exploring themes of deep time, geology, and the environment.

events.title: Spotlight Talk: Earth Matters
events.description: Hear a short talk from one of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh’s Creative Programmes volunteers on their favourite part of the exhibition Earth Matters . Earth Matters marks 300 years since the birth of James Hutton, the Edinburgh-born farmer and writer who revolutionised our understanding of Earth’s creation and the ground beneath us. The exhibition includes work by over 30 artists who have been inspired by Hutton and subsequent trailblazers. At this free event, one of Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh’s amazing volunteers will share with your their knowledge on and enthusiasm for Earth Matters , focusing on one element of the exhibition. A creative partnership with Susanna Beaumont, Design Exhibition Scotland, Earth Matters is supported by players of People’s Postcode Lottery and Edinburgh Geological Society, with special thanks to the James Hutton Institute. The exhibition is part of Edinburgh Science Festival, Edinburgh Art Festival, RSA200: Celebrating Together, and James Hutton Tercentenary 2026.

events.title: Botanics Lates
events.description: Enjoy everything nature has to offer with exclusive after-hours access to the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. Gather for an unforgettable evening of live music, creative workshops and visual art. Explore the beauty of blooms at dusk, with the chance to chat with experts and learn more about our exhibitions and plants. Designed exclusively for over 18s, this is a rare opportunity to dance among the trees, soak up breathtaking city views, and relax on the lawn with refreshing drinks and delicious food. A sanctuary in the heart of the city – gather friends, unwind in nature and enjoy a Friday evening like no other. events.title: Magnus Westwell: Caught Hold of Nothing + Launch Party
events.description: SOLD OUT Caught Hold of Nothing offers a glimpse into a performance work in progress by Scottish artist, performer and director Magnus Westwell. Performing with Océane Robin, Westwell plays live violin to exhaustion, building layered environments in which the body moves through emotional states toward catharsis. Inspired by John Glenday’s poem Vitruvian Man , the work explores absence through cycles of repetition and decay. Music and movement break down and rebuild in tandem, leading to a vulnerable, cathartic, and deeply embodied experience that invites audiences into the liminal space of experimental interdisciplinary performance. The performance will begin the festival’s opening night and launch party. It leads on to a bold late-night celebration in collaboration with Cardion Arts , headlined by rapper and poet Mykki Blanco . Over the past decade, Blanco has evolved from a video-art persona into a pioneering voice in music, blending noise, club, and trap while challenging the boundaries of hip-hop and its dominant narratives. Entering a new chapter, their work continues to push sound and identity into unexpected territory. Taking over the Biscuit Factory late into the night, the opening party will also see DJ sets from 3MR , a Syrian-Scottish multidisciplinary artist and curator of POC-focused events in Scotland, and Sweet Philly , a Dublin-born, Edinburgh-based producer and DJ, and self-styled ‘Queer Club Demon’. An immersive start to the festival, the opening night brings together performance, club culture, and collective experience, setting the tone for a programme defined by bold ideas and boundary-breaking creativity. Doors : 7pm Magnus Westwell : 8pm – 8.30pm (No entry during performance) 3MR : 8.30pm – 10pm Mykki Blanco : 10pm – 11.30pm Sweet Philly : 11.30pm – 1am About Cardion Arts Cardion Arts is a not-for-profit organisation that champions LGBTQIA+ artists through a vibrant programme of exhibitions, performances, workshops and events. The work creates joyful, welcoming and thought-provoking spaces that celebrate queer creativity and foster a sense of belonging, as well as raising vital funds for art, the UK’s only charity dedicated to supporting LGBTQIA+ young people facing homelessness. Caught Hold of Nothing is supported by Creative Scotland, Dance Base, Perth Theatre & Concert Hall, Dundee Rep and Scottish Dance Theatre, a Britten Pears Arts residency, The Mandrake Hotel, PRS Foundation, and the Work Room, and developed at Cove Park. events.title: Artist Talk + Screening: Jillian Edelstein
events.description: Stills hosts a conversation with photographer Jillian Edelstein and curator Tracy Marshall-Grant, presented alongside Jillian Edelstein: Among People , the first major survey exhibition of Edelstein’s work. Curated by Marshall-Grant, the exhibition brings together photographs spanning more than four decades, tracing Edelstein’s distinctive approach to documenting people and communities across the world. This event offers a closer view into the exhibition, as Edelstein reflects on her career, from her early work in South Africa to her internationally recognised practice in London, and shares insight into how she approaches photographing people, relationships and everyday life. The event also includes a screening of Edelstein’s documentary The Water Rats (2022), a quietly observed and deeply touching film following swimmers at Hampstead Heath during lockdown, capturing how a temporary community formed through shared experience, connection, and resilience. Followed by an audience Q&A. Supported by Creative Scotland.

events.title: Common Thread: Sandra George, Wester Hailes + Community Action
events.description: The Community Wellbeing Collective (CWC) hosts a creative gathering to celebrate the work of prolific photographer and community worker Sandra George. George’s photos captured Edinburgh through the 80s and 90s, presenting an intimate portrait of the people she worked with across Wester Hailes and Craigmillar. Her work is held in archive at Craigmillar Now. Led by Craigmillar Now’s lead archivist and CWC member Anna Mayhew, the event offers a close look at the artist’s local photography, alongside a shared meal featuring cyanotype tablecloths, a photography workshop creating a collective installation, and sharing memories of the communities George documented. This is part of a series of Anchor Events: CWC’s monthly explorations bringing together a diverse community connected to Wester Hailes, with local organisations and artists. events.title: Catherine Opie + Del LaGrace Volcano: Radical Imagery Artist Talk
events.description: Co-presented with the Edinburgh International Book Festival, this artist talk explores the radical work of two cult American photographers: Del LaGrace Volcano and Catherine Opie. Volcano’s Love Bites Back is an exhibition of dyke photography, while Opie’s To Be Seen features nearly 80 portraits of those commonly missing from mainstream art history. Both pioneering photographers, they join Kim McAleese, director of EAF, to speak about their work and their portrayal of often invisible communities. Find out more about visiting Edinburgh International Book Festival.

events.title: Tell Me About It: A Hard Labour Human Library Event
events.description: Tell Me About It creates a space for direct one-to-one conversations with people who habitually find others (filmmakers, politicians, journalists) speaking on their behalf… A variation of the Human Library where members of the public – “readers” – can hold direct one on one conversations with people in the role of “books” who will share part of their life story. Imagine entering a library where readers can borrow human beings serving as open books. Then select a book stack that specialises in sex work. “Why did you get into sex work?” “Do you hate your clients?” “Have you ever fallen for a client?” “Do you have a union?” Are there questions you’ve always wanted to ask sex workers? Never had the chance? Developed over several months, the project places consent, autonomy and mutual respect at its heart. Readers and Books are supported through a carefully facilitated process that prioritises psychological safety, boundaries and meaningful dialogue. Created in partnership between Scotland for Decrim , Arika, EAF, and the Human Library® Organisation , the project brings together a diverse collection of Books reflecting the many realities, identities and experiences that exist within sex work. Rather than presenting a single narrative, Tell Me About It invites readers to encounter the richness and complexity of peoples’ lives through respectful conversation, challenging assumptions and sharing space for greater understanding. events.title: BSL Tour: Earth Matters
events.description: Join Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh for a BSL tour of the exhibition Earth Matters. See soil through art. Earth Matters marks 300 years since the birth of James Hutton, the Edinburgh-born geologist, farmer and thinker who revolutionised our understanding of the ground beneath us. Inspired by Hutton and subsequent trailblazers, 30 artists delve into this living ecosystem to reveal its brilliance, beauty and fragility. This exhibition tour is in British Sign Language (BSL), led by Trudi Collier. Meet at the entrance to the exhibition in Inverleith House. If you have any questions, please email creativeprogrammes@rbge.org.uk. This event is part of Edinburgh Deaf Festival.

Bringing together documentary footage, experimental film, and archival material, the screening traces Volcano’s influential role within queer and trans visual culture across several decades. In this joint screening and in-conversation between the two artists, Jackson Kroese weaves Volcano’s work into their ongoing practice of preserving and activating trans histories, considering the archive as a living site of memory, community, and resistance. The event will open space for reflection on how queer and trans lives are documented, shared, and sustained through moving image practices. events.title: Remi Graves: Making Objects Speak
events.description: ‘Outrageously magical things happen when you mess around with a symbol’ David Hammonds, Artist Join poet Remi Graves for a writing workshop exploring the narrative and symbolic potential of objects. Inspired by the artefacts on display in History is A Home the workshop will encourage participants to draw out the memories, symbolisms and possible future lives of objects they hold dear. We’ll lean on texts from Remi’s book coal as well as work by other writers and contemporary artists to explore the lives of objects and where they might take us. Participants are encouraged to bring an object (or image of an object) with them. Please note this event is for BPOC* only (see definition below) to offer a level of collective care and safer space that is not widely available. Event Info → This event is for BPOC (Black people and People of Colour) only. → This event is in Gallery 2 of Custom Lane, which can be found through the back of Gallery 1. There is step-free access to the building from the courtyard, with cobbles underfoot. → This event is seated. If you need a particular kind or placement of seat, please let us know in the “Access Needs” box below. → The event space contains nude photography and illustrated archive material. → Download the Custom Lane Access & Inclusion guide for full venue accessibility information. *BPOC stands for ‘Black people and People of Colour’ and is a self-identifying term. These sessions aim to address and overcome systemic barriers that people face directly or indirectly based on their ethnic or national identities, race or perceived racial identities, or the colour of their skin as per the Equality Act 2010. events.title: Katucha Bento: Effervescent! Human-Body-Nature Beyond Anti-Racism
events.description: Effervescent! is a participatory performance by Katucha Bento exploring embodiment, memory, and our human-nature relation, grounded in Black feminist dreaming. Rooted in the idea of the body as a living archive, the work invites participants to reflect on the crossroads between human, body, and nature: a space where personal and ancestral histories meet and unfold together. Through guided reflection, movement, sound, stillness, and collective presence, the performance asks: where do we meet anti-racism within ourselves and each other? What does it mean to embody anti-racism beyond language alone? In what gestures, rhythms, silences, or acts of care can solidarity, courage, discomfort, and joy emerge? This iteration unfolds in dialogue with poetry and music, a responsive environment of care and possibility, where every participant’s presence contributes to a collective symphony. Effervescent! asks: what starts to bubble and pop into presence when we listen to our bodies, our ancestors, and the land together? The work is performed and created in collaboration with: Shona Inatimi Rue Cooper Victoria Sallam Moyses Gomes Giovanna Iorio Carlo Silva The performance is part of EAF’s ongoing programme around Más Arte Más Accion’s Around a Tree installation bringing artists, scientists, and audiences together to explore human–plant interconnections and biodiversity loss. Event Info → This event is at the Around a Tree table installation, in front of Inverleith House. The event space is outdoors and grassy underfoot. → This event is mixed seated and standing, with stool-style seating available. If you need a particular kind or placement of seat, please let us know in the “Access Needs” box below. → Participants may be invited to engage in gentle movement, vocalisation, and reflection. → The performance includes themes relating to racism, ancestry, memory, and embodied experience. events.title: User Interface: Coded Craft
events.description: User Interface: Coded Craft is a group exhibition bringing together contemporary craft artists and makers whose work sits at the interface between digital technology and traditional handcraft. The artists featured use technology to expand their practices, with a shared focus on looking at how contemporary craft can play a significant role in pursuing ecological innovation for a more sustainable future. The exhibition features work by Jeni Allison, Naomi Mcintosh, Lynne MacLachlan, Liu Qiwei, Aymeric Renoud, Soorin Shin, Sanne Visser, Silvia Weidenbach, and Sandra Wilson. Launching in Edinburgh as part of the festival, the exhibition will go on to tour to arts venues, community centres, high streets and schools across Scotland. events.title: Glasgow Leatherdykes: From History to Today
events.description: What does leather mean to you? What does it mean to build a community around it? Glasgow Leatherdykes are a trans-led group who organise social nights for those who are into or just curious about leather and leather culture, through lesbian bar nights and bootblacking circles. Join them to explore queer history leathercare and bootblacking, and the subculture that has developed around these practices. They will present a history of leatherdyke spaces, before giving attendees a chance to learn some techniques themselves. You do not have to be a lesbian to come to this event (but it helps)! To practice and learn some leathercare on the day, please bring your own boots or leathers! If you don’t own any you’re welcome to just watch if you’d like, or we can pair you up with an instructor so you can practice on someone else’s gear. This event is held in partnership with Edinburgh Deaf Festival. Event Info → This event is in Gallery 2 of Custom Lane, which can be found through the back of Gallery 1. There is step-free access to the building from the courtyard, with cobbles underfoot. → This event is mixed seated and standing. If you need a particular kind or placement of seat, please let us know in the “Access Needs” box when booking tickets. → This event has BSL interpretation, with two interpreters. → The event space events.title: Level Up: Block Party
events.description: Level Up is a social gathering celebrating the life and legacy of Sandra George through music, movement, food, and collective joy. Inspired by George’s community-rooted philosophy, “Stop making assumptions about people / Start from the level people are based” , the evening creates space for connection, togetherness, release, and highlights why being in spaces with good vibes levels you up. Sandra George was a Black social-documentary photographer, youth worker, and community organiser whose work centred care, creativity, and empowerment within Craigmillar. Presented in collaboration with Craigmillar Now and City Art Centre, Level Up brings her archive and ethos into the present through an evening of celebration, sound, and community gathering. Through music, dance, and collective presence, the event reflects George’s belief that art and community have the power to uplift and transform, while celebrating joy as a vital form of care, resistance, and connection. DJ Lineup: CC TIME : CC invites you to experience a musical journey rooted in reflection and soul. Her style blends the hopeless romanticism of 70s–90s R&B and Soul with the nostalgia of a 2010s college fantasy and the vibrant disco-infused R&B of the 2020s. Her sets are filled with an endless giddiness that makes you feel like dancing in the street or squealing in your bedroom waiting for that phone call. In the words of DJ legend Gemma Cairney, she is a selector. LUCKYBABE : Born of Guyanese and Irish roots in the Scottish Highlands, LuckyBabe is a DJ whose sets blend deep feeling with high-impact energy. A resident of PonyBoy and Kin.x, and co-founder of gullygully, and Serve!, she brings together boldness, emotion, and sonic precision on every dance floor. Classically trained on the recorder, her musicality runs through every mix. RIA : Ria is an Edinburgh based DJ and multi-hyphenate artist, from South London. A resident of Femmergy, she is known for her mixes that feature groovy riddims, heavy on percussion, catchy basslines and a fun remix selection. Weaving in some Baile Funk, Afro House and an old school R&B or Hip Hop edit or two expect lots of energy and lots of heat! SIMBA : Simba is an Edinburgh-based DJ and creative multi-hyphenate playing for the queers, the chronically online and the aunties who know every word to My Neck My Back. Glossy nostalgia, pussy poppin’, main character fuel. Runway or dancefloor, you decide. Known to serve a look with a soundtrack to match, Simba spins sounds for the body, the brains and the bad bitches. events.title: Creative Workshop: Egyptian Ceramics
events.description: Join writer and ceramicist Mohamed Tonsy at the National Museum of Scotland to explore Egyptian ceramics and make your own clay piece in this hands-on workshop. The session will look in detail at ‘olla – terracotta water vessels – and particularly the filters that were hidden inside. These functional filters were often richly decorated with geometric designs and written blessings. In this hands-on workshop you can use these humble but beautiful objects as inspiration to create your own decorative clay piece. Mohamed Tonsy is an Edinburgh-based Egyptian writer and ceramicist. He moved to Edinburgh to complete his PhD in creative writing, taking up ceramics. Ceramics provides an additional language to express his experiences and intersectional identity, bridging Arabic and English. He has worked with our curatorial team to explore the National Museums collections, through the lived experience of contemporary Egyptian communities.

events.title: BIG SPELL
events.description: BIG SPELL is a day of sharing centred on Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop members, celebrating the infinite possibilities, the circular community, and commitment to practice. The event takes inspiration from the regenerative nature of working at ESW, where each person’s ideas, efforts, and skills feed in to create the ongoing momentum for the whole community of practice. This has brought to mind imagery of the Ouroboros (the snake eating itself), an icon with meanings across multiple cultures and within disciplines from alchemy to psychology: all understanding the power of self-reflexivity, and the idea that matter and energy are never lost, but perpetually change form. These ideas reflect the chance for a certain form of stability within uncertainty: a confidence in the ability we have together to create and support each other, as sure as the cycles of the sun. Join ESW in the melting pot of ideas, of conversation, skill-sharing, and creation: a bubbling witch’s brew. Come along for this free whole building event sharing the work of over 40 artists through exhibitions, open studios, and talks. events.title: Davi Pontes + Sebastião Abreu: Serial Component
events.description: Serial Component is a choreographic research project and performance developed by Brazilian artist Davi Pontes, unfolding across three episodes. Each presents a specific bodily vocabulary through collaborations with invited performers, navigating intimate and fragmentary exchanges. Exploring notions of the archive and questioning the transmission of choreographic codes inherited from Western traditions, the work invites us to think of the choreographic gesture not as something fixed or predetermined, but rather as a flow. Continuing research initiated with philosopher Denise Ferreira da Silva around the concept of Black Ecologies, the work proposes heat transfer as an alternative to the Western model of dance: an internal energy that moves through difference, without one body becoming another or losing its attributes. The performance is developed through a collaborative project between EAF and Pinacoteca de São Paulo, where the performance will continue later this year. The performance is part of EAF’s ongoing programme around Más Arte Más Accion’s Around a Tree installation bringing artists, scientists, and audiences together to explore human–plant interconnections events.title: National Union of Journalists: Representing Communities Panel Discussion
events.description: Join EAF and the National Union of Journalists and guests for a discussion event to discuss the social, cultural and ethical issues of working within communities. The legacy of Sandra George’s life, community work and photographic archive provides the basis which to examine how the influence of social class, gender, and racial politics can shape community based practice. Reflecting on Sandra George’s work, the panel will discuss through their own experiences and principles, what should be considered as best practice when undertaking community projects. The event is being supported by the National Union of Journalists in celebration of the life and work of Sandra George as a member, and their continuing commitment to both professional standards and working towards building a better and fairer UK media, representative of all. Audiences will also have the opportunity to ask questions and discuss the current work of the National Union of Journalists. The panel includes: Alicia Bruce, Arusa Quereshi, Christian Noelle Charles. Chaired by Natasha Hirst. Event Info: → This event is on Floor 5 of the City Art Centre, which is accessible by lift from the ground floor. → This event is fully seated. events.title: Artist Talk: Sadao Hasegawa
events.description: Join EAF for an artist talk diving into the work of Sadao Hasegawa, one of post-war Japan’s most influential gay fetish artists. Showing in Scotland for the first time, EAF exhibition Carnal Desires reveals the fantastical queer worlds of Hasegawa’s paintings: where idealised male forms encounter mythic creatures, hybrid animals, and divine bodies unbound by earthly limits. Featuring unearthed pieces from the archives of Tokyo’s Gallery Naruyama, many of which have never been shown before in the UK, this talk will celebrate the life and legacy of Hasegawa, and the impact of his erotic queer cosmos on artists for years to come. The talk will be led by Dr Cole Collins and Dr Patrick Carland-Echavarria , two scholars whose work sits at the intersection of queer art history, translation, and cultural exchange. Collins is a researcher, editor and writer specialising in queer art and Dada, and has chaired sessions for EAF and Edinburgh International Book Festival on queer art, literature, and film. Carland-Echavarria is a cultural historian whose research focuses on queer literature and media in postwar Japan, and whose recent curatorial work includes the exhibition The First Homosexuals: The Birth of a New Identity, 1869–1939 . Event Info → This event is in Gallery 2 of Custom Lane, which can be found through the back of Gallery 1. There is step-free access to the building from the courtyard, with cobbles underfoot. → This event is seated. If you need a particular kind or placement of seat, please let us know in the “Access Needs” box below. → The exhibition features paintings that graphically depict nudity, sex, and fetish practices, including bondage and beastiality. → Download the Custom Lane Access & Inclusion guide for full venue accessibility information. In collaboration with Gallery Naruyama. Supported by National Center for Art Research Japan, Japan House London, and Art Fund’s Jonathan Ruffer Curatorial Grant. events.title: Morphological Murmurations
events.description: Morphological Murmurations is a multisensory installation engaging audiences with language, embodied communication, neurodivergence, artificial intelligence (AI) and models of animal behaviour, created by lead artist Theodore Koterwas. The artwork places visitors within the space of a Large Language Model, an AI system designed to understand and analyse human language, where a flock of artificial agents respond to their movements, visually and sonically activating words. This is language, not assembled through computational logic, but through patterns of bodies working together. Through the intuition of movement, muscle memory and spatial awareness, the visitor explores the environment of a putative “other mind” (the LLM) through an alternative model of how embodied minds (birds) coordinate movement and create meaning with their bodies.

events.description: Update: We’re sorry to let you know that the upcoming event is no longer going ahead. Apologies for the inconvenience, and thank you for your understanding. Refunds will be issued in full to your original payment method within five days. Falastin Film Festival’s expansive programme dedicated to Palestinian and Lebanese artists continues from 27—30 August. You may also be interested in: → Activating Archives: Reclaiming Colonial Images → South Lebanon: Homage to the Frontliners → Gaza: Against The Perfect Victim You can explore the full programme at falastinfilmfest.com Join cultural historian + curator Ellie Armon Azoulay and Mo’min Swaitat of Majazz Project and Palestinian Sound Archive for a conversation in response to Metal Memories: Sounds of the Palestinian Streets . Centred around rare field recordings of Palestinian and Bedouin wedding traditions, the discussion will explore sound as a carrier of memory, resistance, and collective cultural identity. Reflecting on the role of archives, storytelling, and sonic culture within their practices, they will each consider how music, celebration, and oral histories can preserve experiences of community and belonging across displacement and occupation. The conversation will also engage with the political stakes of listening: how sound can bear witness, be interrupted, or be lost, and what it means to attend to a sonic landscape shaped by both celebration and rupture. events.title: Activating Archives: Reclaiming Colonial Images
events.description: This programme brings together two films that reclaim archival images from the colonial gaze, transforming records of domination into sites of resistance, memory, and political intervention. By revisiting and reworking historical footage, the programme asks how archives can be activated to contest official histories and recover what colonial image-making sought to erase. Screened as part of Falastin Film Festival (27—30 August). About the films Kamal Aljafari: UNDR The camera’s eye returns obsessively to the same places, a vertical perspective that imposes control, the possession of archaeological sites, stones lying for thousands years in the desert. The places it observes, however, are not deserted: we see, as if glimpsed from afar, the peasants working the land, themselves transformed into landscape. Something disturbs the stillness of the place: explosions on land and in the sea prepare the ground for new cities with new names, new forests. This landscape is transformed into a scenography of appropriation. Diana Allan: Partition Partition fuses archival footage from the British occupation of Palestine with audio recorded of Palestinian refugees in Lebanon. Silent films gathered in imperial collections hold histories that have barely been told. Recovering Palestinian presence through story, voice and song, unraveling colonial pasts through soundscapes of the precarious present, Partition is a meditation on what bodies remember and empires forget. After the screenings there will be a Q+A with directors Kamal Aljafari and Diana Allan.

events.title: Lawrence Abu Hamdan: Radical Listening Artist Talk
events.description: Visionary artist Lawrence Abu Hamdan makes use of sound to investigate that which is not seen, but heard. In 2023, he founded the organisation Earshot, dedicated to the study of audio for human rights and environmental advocacy. In this artist talk, he discusses combining the role of artist and investigator and offers an introduction to Earshot’s transformation of sound into a tool of justice. Find out more about visiting Edinburgh International Book Festival.

events.title: Gaza: What Still Grows
events.description: Set against the backdrop of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza, these three films are united by an insistence on creating life under conditions designed to destroy it. Whether tending the land, building new technologies of care, or performing for children, they present creation not as an escape from genocide, but as a refusal to let it define the limits of Palestinian life. Screened as part of Falastin Film Festival (27—30 August). About the films Woroud Alqassas: Seeds & Roots Here, where gunpowder is mixed with soil, Seba kneels to cleanse the soil from the ashes of war, watering it with her small cup trying to revive memories buried in the seeds. Besides her stands her grandfather, Abu Diaa, his voice is rough as the land, rooted like an old olive tree. He knows the land and the land knows him. He teaches her that planting is a promise of life despite all forms of death. Together, they help their land to breathe again, each green leaf they grow together becomes a new birth certificate. Maria Marone: Rendered In Light When Mosab, a skilled software engineer, is separated from his wife and children as they evacuate Gaza for emergency medical care, he’s left behind with only uncertainty and a laptop. Alone in a city under siege, he begins building something extraordinary: a virtual reality program designed to help survivors of genocide cope with mental trauma. As genocide rages around him, Mosab immerses himself in creating digital worlds of calm and reflection. The film follows his journey as he balances the emotional weight of his own loneliness with a relentless drive to serve others. Through acts of kindness and innovation, he finds a way to preserve his own mental health, turning grief into action, and despair into purpose. Mai Saad + Ahmed Al Danaf: One More Show Amidst the devastation of the genocide carried by Israel in Gaza, a group of circus performers refuse to let despair take center stage. One More Show follows The Free Gaza troupe; Youssef, Batout, Ismail, Mohamed and Just, after being displaced from northern to southern Gaza , as they turn their craft into an act of defiance, resilience, and hope. As death hovers in the background, the troupe performs for children in shelters and on the streets, offering moments of joy in the darkest of times. After the screenings there will be a Q+A with the directors.

events.title: Ahmad Ghossein: All This Victory
events.description: Lebanon, July 2006. War is raging between Hezbollah and Israel. During a 24h ceasefire, Marwan heads out in search of his father who refused to leave his Southern village and leaves his wife Rana preparing alone their immigration to Canada. Marwan finds no traces of his father and the ceasefire is quickly broken, forcing him to take shelter in Najib’s house, his father’s friend. Marwan finds himself trapped under the rain of bombs with Najib and a group of elders, friends of his father. Tension rises inside and outside of the house. Suddenly, a group of Israeli soldiers enter the first floor. The next three days sees the situation spiral out of control. Screened as part of Falastin Film Festival (27—30 August). Followed by an online Q&A with the director.

events.title: Parallel Time
events.description: How do we tell the stories of our prisoners? Across essay film, fiction, and documentary, this programme explores storytelling as a form of resistance against the silencing and isolation imposed by incarceration. Drawing from Walid Daqqa’s notion of parallel time—the suspended temporality imposed by colonial imprisonment, where prisoners are severed from the linear time of the outside world—the films reveal prison not only as a site of confinement, but as a space where culture, thought, and connection continue to exist. In the context of ongoing struggles around political imprisonment, including the Filton 25 case here in the UK, the programme also asks how narratives of prisoners are constructed, challenged, and reclaimed. Screened as part of Falastin Film Festival (27—30 August). About the films Samira Makki: When Solid Turns To Dust, Or A Note On Liquidity From Palestine This video essay explores liquidity, and its intermittent leaks, as a poetic and political proposition informing anti-colonial struggles. The essay takes its cue from a letter that political prisoner and martyr Walid Daqqa wrote in 2005 where he theorized Parallel Time under Zionist captivity at a high-security facility known as the Gilboa prison. More than a decade later, the same prison became a marker of the historical escape orchestrated by six Palestinian prisoners. Importantly, the escape became an attestation of the possibility of transgression: the Zionist project, in its high-security doctrine and carceral apparatus, are but an illusion made up of dust, as Mahmoud Al-Arda reiterated. The escape triggered the anxiety of the settler-colony not only as it denoted a leak from the ostensibly impenetrable Parallel Time. Rather, the leak expresses an outright commitment to futurity where there is seemingly none. Rakan Mayasi: Bonboné It is thought that wars and conflicts conquer the essence of body and soul, like the heaving of waves on a rough sea. An imprisoned Palestinian from the resistance forces is serving his time in an Israeli jail. Yearning to see his offspring, he contrives a plot with the help of his spouse. Will his attempt pan out as planned? Al Jazeera: Walid Daqqa: A Parallel Life This is the story of Walid Daqqa, one of the longest-serving Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails, told by his immediate family and in voice recordings he made behind bars. From a sharp-minded boy in 1948 Palestine to a clandestine PFLP organiser sentenced to life imprisonment, Daqqa turns his cell into a classroom, a think tank and, eventually, a wedding venue when he marries Sanaa Salama inside Ashkelon prison. Through intimate testimonies from family, former prisoners and his lawyer, the film explores Walid’s idea of “parallel time” – living both under “tonnes of concrete” and beyond the walls. It recounts the smuggling of his sperm, the birth of his daughter, Milad, and his powerful message to her: hate oppression, not people. As cancer consumes him and Israel refuses his release, Milad’s final chant, “Freedom for our prisoners. For my father”, echoes a struggle that outlives Walid Daqqa’s life. Following the screening will be a Q+A with Diala Ayesh. Diala Ayesh is a Palestinian lawyer and human rights defender dedicated to advocating for the rights of prisoners and detainees. Her work focuses on providing legal representation to political detainees, visiting prisoners held in Israeli prisons, and documenting violations against them. She has continued this work during the period of intensified restrictions and near-total isolation imposed on Palestinian prisoners following the outbreak of the war on Gaza. Because of her human rights work, Diala has faced harassment and arrest by both the Palestinian Authority and Israeli authorities. On January 17, 2024, she was arrested by Israeli forces and placed under administrative detention without charge or trial. During her nearly year-long detention, she endured mistreatment and prolonged isolation before being released on January 14, 2025. In recognition of her commitment to defending freedom of expression and human rights, Diala received the 2024 Freedom of Expression Award from Index on Censorship.

events.title: Gaza: Against The Perfect Victim
events.description: Inspired by Mohammed El-Kurd’s critique of the “perfect victim,” this programme brings together two films that refuse the narrow roles so often assigned to Palestinian men. Across life before and during Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza, they offer intimate portraits of men in all their contradictions – playful, vulnerable, stubborn, imperfect, and deeply ordinary – insisting on the right to be seen as fully human rather than as symbols to be judged. Screened as part of Falastin Film Festival (27—30 August). About the films Bisan Owda: Free Fish Free Fish is an intimate short documentary filmed entirely in Gaza during one of the deadliest years in recent history. The film follows two brothers, Mohammad and Ahmad Kaloob, separated by siege and displacement, yet bound by the sea. Mohammad, displaced in Khan Younis with his two young daughters, fishes from the South and tries to find alternatives for the boat and net he lost in the bombing of Gaza Seaport. Ahmad, still in the North under total blockade, risks his life each morning near the Al-Shate’e refugee camp, what was once a livelihood is now a daily act of survival, the coastline is militarized, boats are shot at and hunger is used as a weapon of war. And yet, the brothers return to the sea. They cast their nets and their memories, into waters that no longer offer freedom, but still carry meaning. Fishing becomes a fragile ritual of resistance, of connection, of presence. The film also follows Rami, Mohammad’s teenage nephew, who lost his twin brother during the genocide and now fishes alone. Through him, Free Fish becomes not just a story of survival, but of grief, inheritance, and the quiet defiance of those who refuse to disappear. Mahmoud Nabil Ahmed: Gazan Tales In the heart of the beloved Gaza Strip, four men navigate through divergent paths in pursuit of their own definitions of existence, intertwining their fates amidst the complexities of life, love, and survival. As the film unfolds, viewers are immersed in the daily lives of these men, observing how they navigate their routines alongside their families in their beloved city.

events.title: South Lebanon: Homage to the Frontliners
events.description: This programme traces the enduring histories of occupation and war in South Lebanon, from 1978 to the present, through films that bear witness to both armed resistance and the quieter, everyday labour of remaining. Framed by acts of return – to liberated villages, to destroyed homes, to sites of memory – the programme honours those who fought on the frontlines and those who, between intervals, continued to care for the land, preserving life and sustaining the possibility of return as acts of resistance in themselves. Screened as part of Falastin Film Festival (27—30 August). About the films Randa Chahal Sabbag: Soha, Surviving Hell Originally from South Lebanon – a region she had always known to be under Israeli occupation – Souha Bechara attempted to assassinate General Lahd, commander of the South Lebanon Army, an auxiliary force of Israel. Seriously injured, he narrowly escaped death. Souha, meanwhile, was imprisoned and tortured. She was 21 years old and would spend ten years in Khiam camp, six of them in complete solitary confinement. On 24 May 2000, after 23 years of occupation, Israel withdrew from southern Lebanon. The Khiam camp was stormed by the crowd… The film traces Souha’s return to her village of Deir Mimas, to the Khiam camp, and to the very place where she attempted to assassinate General Lahd, showing her reunion with former detainees from the Khiam camp. Batoul Faour: The Bunker, The Barrack & The Base Towards the end of the Second World War, French and British forces fortified the Khiam Marjayoun valley and its surrounding villages in the South of Lebanon through a comprehensive military scheme. At the core of this scheme were three structures – a hospital bunker, an airbase, and a military barracks. After the retreat of the allies came the establishment of the State of Israel, and the political turmoil that would follow. The Bunker, The Barracks, and The Bas e is a portrait of collective remembrance in a landscape where invasion and occupation have shaped the lives of many generations. It explores the three architectural sites through the experiences of those who have come to inhabit them beyond their militaristic ambitions. The relationship of these sites to the land, to each other, and to the border that mediates them is rife with contradiction, and yet what binds them are the histories—memories, spirits, outlooks—of those that have learned to make a life through, with, and despite them. Fatima Joumaa: From My Mother’s Novel Fatima, Layla’s daughter, after documenting the war in South-lebanon, returns to her home to hide within the folds of her mother’s book. As she uncovers her mother’s hidden writings, she discovers the echoes of Southern Lebanon’s grief during the war. Through Layla’s words and her own photographs, the film weaves a tapestry of personal and collective memory. Joude Bazzoun: 66 Days Set in the village of Bazouriye in South Lebanon, 66 Days follows filmmaker Joude Bazzoun’s return to her homeland after witnessing Israel’s 2024 onslaught on Lebanon from abroad. Through intimate conversations with her family, Joude uncovers the losses they have suffered. The film reflects on the importance of memory and tradition by exploring the ritual of a card game and family gatherings. 66 Days quietly resists erasure, preserving the family’s stories and heritage while celebrating the defiant joy found in simple family traditions. After the screening there will be a Q+A with the directors.

events.title: Lawrence Abu Hamdan: Zifzafa
events.description: Sound performance Zifzafa , named for an Arabic word describing a wind that shakes everything in its path, centres on the Israeli-occupied Syrian Golan Heights, where 30 planned wind turbines will flood the region with a relentless mechanical roar. Framed as a ‘green’ energy project, the turbines weaponise sound itself, unsettling and exhausting local life. Lawrence Abu Hamdan, artist and founder of Earshot, the first non-profit dedicated to audio for justice, whose investigations have informed landmark legal cases, brings this research to the stage. The performance is scored by Busher Kanj Abu Saleh, who performs live together with saxophonist Amr Mdah and Renate Lurdesa Baumane. Through sound and visual models, they turn the imposed noise into an act of resistance: transforming acoustic violence into something that can be witnessed, felt, and collectively opposed. The performance is programmed in collaboration with Falastin Film Festival, and accompanied by an exhibition at The Common Guild in Glasgow, running 20 Aug—17 October. Join us after the performance at Leith Theatre to close out the festival with a pop-up bar hosted by festival partners, Whitebox.
